<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`, `packages/spec/src/automation/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via intervalMs (literal, a string literal in typedAliasHint))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via intervalMs (literal, a string literal in typedAliasHint))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via intervalMs (literal, a string literal in typedAliasHint))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via intervalMs (literal, a string literal in typedAliasHint))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`, `packages/spec/src/automation/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5e54edfbd3f293be0157d78ff5df48634185032b` — the merge of head `bdc95ace88d92c914d25a04dba2cd2725ac1baab` into base `eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5e54edfbd3f293be0157d78ff5df48634185032b && git checkout 5e54edfbd3f293be0157d78ff5df48634185032b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7 bdc95ace88d92c914d25a04dba2cd2725ac1baab && git checkout -B drift-repro eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7 && git merge --no-ff bdc95ace88d92c914d25a04dba2cd2725ac1baab

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `532b289f434b6d945b8c5c09cd59d6fdfc261eeb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/31224-flow-start-config-refusals.md, packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json, packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-start-config-refusals.test.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-start-config-refusals.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/index.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/schedule-reader-spec-parity.test.ts, skills/objectstack-automation/references/_index.md + packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/schedule-trigger.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/time-relative-trigger.ts, packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/time-relative-trigger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-read-decorations.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin-extension-api.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.ts, examples/app-todo/src/flows/task.flow.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/fixtures/schedule-organization-fixture.ts, packages/cli/test/fixtures/option-b-collection-zoo.ts, skills/objectstack-automation/references/examples-flows.md, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, content/docs/references/automation/time-relative-trigger.mdx, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, hotcrm `6961ab1` src/**/flows/*.flow.ts (31 files)

Inputs read: card #31224 body and every comment (triage 6711648543, claim 6712039823, plan 6712129038, seat rulings 6712144718 and 6714195854, dev reports 6713825906, 6716296533 and the B1 report 6717473839); PR #31376 body, file list (9 paths) and `git diff origin/main...532b289f` (merge-base `c2bc76e3`, +337/-0); the check-runs on `532b289f` at three reads; for shape only, the merged siblings #31287 and #31337 with their records and changesets. Judged on the committed tree, not the PR body's account of it; nothing was built or run, and the corpus statements below are greps of `objectstack` at `532b289f` and of hotcrm `main` at `6961ab1` (read through the GitHub API). Face and tier: `reviewFace` on the PR's 9 paths answers face `schema` (schema hits `flow-start-config-refusals.ts`, `flow.zod.ts`, `automation/index.ts`; rules hit `skills/objectstack-automation/references/_index.md`, a governed path), the paths deciding before the `yes (narrowing)` declaration would — the same `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, `recordCarriesDesignJudgment` true, and the `Scope:` line above holds every hit; this record is served at that tier on both faces' questions (the schema file against its ruling and first consumer, the narrowing against the published spec).

### ① Derived judgments

**Parity with `normalizeSchedule` — exact, by reading.** `flowStartScheduleReadsNothing` (`flow-start-config-refusals.ts`) is `normalizeSchedule` (`schedule-trigger.ts:597`) branch for branch: `null`/`undefined` (deliberately answered "not judged" rather than "reads nothing"), string trimmed and empty, non-object, `type` read only when a string, the cron arm's `(expression && expression) || (cron && cron)` truthiness, the interval arm's `(intervalMs) || (every)` with `!intervalMs || intervalMs at most 0`, the once arm's `at` string, and the fall-through. The "first candidate present decides" precedence (`{ intervalMs: -1, every: 60000 }` reads nothing; `{ intervalMs: 0, every: 60000 }` reads `every`) is the same expression on both sides, and the 34-row pin in `schedule-reader-spec-parity.test.ts` holds the equivalence as a CI fact in both directions (including `{ every: NaN }`, the `{ type: 7 }` non-string type and the `{ dialect, source }` envelope). Both runtime readers go through this one function: `ScheduleTrigger.start` (`schedule-trigger.ts:756`, `binding.schedule ?? binding.config.schedule`) and `TimeRelativeTrigger.start` (`time-relative-trigger.ts:399`, `normalizeSchedule(binding.schedule) ?? daily 08:00 UTC`), with the engine lifting `config.schedule` onto both bindings (`plugin-extension-api.ts:282,304`). So on the untyped arm there is no false refusal of a schedule the runtime binds and no false acceptance of one it drops.

**The typed arm is NOT parity, and the ruling says so.** A typed object is judged by the published `ScheduleSchema` (`job.zod.ts`: `z.object` per variant, not strict; `expression: CronExpressionInputSchema`, which accepts a non-blank string or a `{ dialect: 'cron', source }` envelope; `timezone` an `iana_time_zone` member, default `'UTC'`; `intervalMs` a positive int; `at` an ISO datetime). Two typed shapes the runtime binds today are therefore refused: `{ type: 'interval', every: 60000 }` and `{ type: 'cron', cron: '0 8 * * *' }` (the alias is read inside the typed branch of `normalizeSchedule`; the PR's own parity rows for these two shapes read `false`, so the diff documents that the runtime binds them). The seat ruled option (a) in 6714195854 — "an object schedule that carries `type` is judged against `ScheduleSchema`" — so the refusal is sanctioned; it is named here because the ruling's reason ("this card enforces what does not run, not what does") does not cover these two shapes, and because the changeset's ADR-0087 reason states the opposite (② below). Census: 0 instances of either shape in `objectstack` source, docs, skills or hotcrm (the one `{ type: 'interval', every: '5m' }` is `flow-trigger-kind.test.ts:51`, which calls the resolver on a raw object and never parses `FlowSchema`). The other typed refusals are of shapes that never run: a non-IANA `timezone` is copied through by `normalizeSchedule`, then `computeTickWindow` (`schedule-trigger.ts:230-236`) catches croner's throw and answers no window, and `job.zod.ts`'s own header records the cron adapter's FAILED TO SCHEDULE for the same value; `intervalMs: 0`, a missing `expression`, a non-ISO `at` and an unknown `type` all read nothing. The envelope case (passes the schema, reader reads nothing) is correctly caught by the second judgment.

**`config.filter` beside `config.timeRelative` — no reader exists.** The sweep reads its row filter from the descriptor only (`time-relative-trigger.ts:212`, `...(desc.filter ?? {})` ANDed with the date range); `deriveTriggerBinding` lifts `condition`, `schedule`, `organization` and `timeRelative.object`, never `config.filter`; the published descriptor schema (`time-relative-trigger.zod.ts`) teaches `filter` inside `timeRelative`. Every other `config.filter` reader in the repo is a CRUD node's (`validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts:1188` reads `filter.id.$in` on `ROW_ADDRESSING_CRUD_NODE_TYPES`; `validate-empty-combinators.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts:1102`), and the record-change and api triggers read `condition`, not `filter`. The refusal fires only when `timeRelative` is present, so a record-change flow's start node keeps any stray `filter` it carries, and a sweep whose filter sits inside the descriptor (the showcase `showcase_task_due_reminder`, the docs, the skill) is untouched. Nit (should-fix, wording): the guard is `config.timeRelative !== undefined`, while the resolver's is `!= null && typeof === 'object'` (`flow-trigger-kind.ts`), so `timeRelative: null` beside a `filter` is refused with a sweep message for a flow the engine does not treat as a sweep; `isRecord(config.timeRelative)` would align the two.

**Top-level start nodes only — right.** Every reader picks `flow.nodes.find(type === 'start')` on the top-level list (`plugin-extension-api.ts:201`, `flow-trigger-kind.ts`), region bodies live inside container `config` and never hold a start node, and the test pins that a non-start node's `config.schedule` is not judged. A second top-level start node is judged too (its config is never read, so this over-refuses harmlessly, and item C already refuses a second start at lint).

**Doors, and which keep.** The rule is in `FlowSchema.superRefine`, so it reaches every door that parses a flow: `defineFlow`/`defineStack` (`flow.zod.ts:1986`), `os lint/validate/build` (`validate-flow-region-shape.ts:121`, `flow-undeclared-cycle.ts:61`), the metadata save door for EVERY state including drafts (`protocol-save.ts:1424-1428`, `resolveOverlaySchema(...).safeParse`, refused 422 with the issue path `nodes.0.config.schedule`), the publish and restore doors that go through the save door's judge, and engine registration (`flow-definitions.ts:212`, `FlowSchema.parse(converted)` AFTER the ADR-0087 conversion replay). A stored flow carrying a refused shape: at cold boot `registerFlow` throws and the engine records the refusal per flow (`recordFlowRefusal`, `flow-definitions.ts:241`; `flowRefusals` map, not a boot abort), the read path serves it with `_diagnostics.valid: false` (`metadata-diagnostics.ts:312-337`, a `safeParse`, never a refusal on read), and the next active save is refused until the author applies the cure. That is the same migration profile as every earlier parse narrowing (#4001 closed shapes, #4277), and the refused flow was unbound or on the silent default before, so no running automation stops; the PR body names the door set correctly. The draft door is where the parse altitude bites (④ and the designer finding in ③).

**Message, location and cure — right, two nits.** Path `['nodes', i, 'config', 'filter' | 'schedule']` is the authored location (pinned). The filter message names the reader, the consequence (every record in the window) and the move. The typed message quotes the first `ScheduleSchema` issue with its sub-path (`schedule.timezone`, pinned) and lists the three typed spellings and the bare string; the untyped message names the three readable keys and the two consequences (unbound schedule flow, daily 08:00 UTC sweep). Nits: the schedule messages speak of "a schedule flow" or "a sweep" even on a record-change or api start node that carries a stray `schedule` key (nothing reads it there; the refusal is still of a dead key, the sentence is just wider than the case); and for a sweep the refused cadence is one the runtime silently replaces, not one that stops the flow — the message says so, correctly.

**Census — nothing shipped, example, dogfood or hotcrm is refused.** `filter` beside `timeRelative`: 0 in `examples/**`, `packages/**`, `skills/**`, `content/docs/**` and hotcrm (hotcrm has no `timeRelative` flow at all). Start-node `schedule` values: bare strings in `examples/app-todo/src/flows/task.flow.ts:57,167` and seven hotcrm flows (`campaign-completion`, `contract-expiration`, `contract-renewal`, `forecast-snapshot`, `opportunity-stagnation`, `quote-expiration`, `task-due-reminder`), all accepted; typed `{ type: 'interval', intervalMs: 60000 }` (`app-showcase/.../flows/index.ts:445`), typed crons in `schedule-organization-fixture.ts:74` and `option-b-collection-zoo.ts:324` (with `timezone: 'UTC'`), all valid under `ScheduleSchema` and readable. The skill and docs teach `{ type: 'cron', expression }` and `timeRelative.filter` only (`examples-flows.md:31,98`, `flows.mdx:2802,2845,2918`, `time-relative-trigger.mdx:42-59`). `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded success on this head.

**Tests.** The 10 spec cases pin the filter refusal and both acceptances, each accepted schedule form (bare string, three typed, five untyped aliases), the IANA refusal at the parse with its sub-path, four `ScheduleSchema` refusals, seven reads-nothing refusals, the envelope, `null`/absent/non-start not judged, and the precedence. The parity file pins 33 shapes plus the absent case. The ledgers (`api-surface`, `export-origins`) carry exactly the three new names at their sorted positions, `FlowStartConfigRefusal` as `(interface)` matching its declaration; `check:generated` runs in `Lint & Repo Gates`, success on this head.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `@objectstack/spec: minor` — right.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor` on a moved package; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (level axis): `narrowed` must grade a moved package `minor` and sit beside a `(narrowing)` arm — both hold; `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — right.** The value answers whether the diff widens a public surface (`clause2-line.mjs`); `@objectstack/spec/automation` gains three exports, so `yes`; the parse refuses two shapes it accepted, so `(narrowing)`. Same reading the item-C record adopted for `FLOW_NODE_UNREACHABLE` (and the precedent `46d2b6503`). Body and changeset agree; `reviewFace` maps the arm to this face.
- **`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — right.** "A value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`" (step 3).
- **`Skills-docs: none — …` — present in body and changeset, and the reason checks out** (census above: skills and docs teach only the accepted forms). The `_index.md` regeneration follows mechanically from importing `job.zod.ts` into the flow closure (its imports are `value-domain.zod.ts`, `hook-body.zod.ts`, `schedule-organization.zod.ts`, which are exactly the four added rows), and `check:skill-refs` is inside the green `check:generated`.
- **BREAKING banner and the `!` in `fix(spec)!:` — consistent**, no script reads the title `!` (item-C record, unchanged tree).
- **MUST-FIX — the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is contradicted by the changeset's own body, and by ADR-0087 D2, for the filter arm.** The gate defines the category as "REFUSED when the changeset's own body carries a migration prescription … instructions for rewriting a consumer's code" (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, the honesty table). This changeset carries one: "**FROM** `config: { timeRelative: { … }, filter: { status: 'active' } }` **TO** `config: { timeRelative: { …, filter: { status: 'active' } } }`", plus "move the filter into `timeRelative.filter`" under "What an author does". The gate did not see it only because its detector reads a FROM/TO pair with an arrow on one line, a line-initial vertical pair, or a rewrite table (`FROM_TO_LABEL_RE`, `VERTICAL_FROM_RE`), and this spelling is mid-line bold with no arrow — the detector-miss class the gate's own docblock records for #8277 and #18745, not an acceptance. The contradiction is also substantive: the filter arm is a lossless field move of an authored key to its declared home, which is the D2 scope by name ("renames, alias removals, field moves"), and ADR-0087's policy paragraph says a lossless break lands as a chain step (a `retiredFromLoadPath` conversion plus the D3 semantic entry) in the same release — and `registerFlow` replays conversions BEFORE the parse (`flow-definitions.ts:191-212`), so a conversion is exactly what would keep an already-stored flow of that shape loading instead of landing in `flowRefusals`. The marker's own prose ("there is no rewrite that keeps what the author meant in every case") is true of the schedule arm and false of the filter arm. The siblings differ materially: C's and D's changesets carry no rewrite because none preserves intent, which is why their `no-migration-prescription` stood. Two cures, the seat's choice (③): register the filter move as a D2 conversion with its fixture and semantic entry and write `registered (ids)`; or, if the seat rules that an undeclared key on an open-record `config` is no D2 surface (the #4277 class), write that ruling into the marker's reason and remove the FROM/TO rewrite spelling the category forbids while keeping the one-line cure — a seat ruling, because AGENTS.md step 3 ("breaking changesets must carry their migration … FROM → TO") and the category's definition pull in opposite directions for this class and neither sibling faced it. Either way the shipped text changes, and a factual error in a released changeset is amendable only by a dedicated docs PR (AGENTS.md, `CHANGELOG.md` row).
- **Should-fix (text): the same marker says a typed schedule "the published `ScheduleSchema` refuses … never bound as written".** `{ type: 'interval', every: 60000 }` and `{ type: 'cron', cron: '…' }` bind today (① above, and the PR's own parity rows). The sentence should say what is true: typed objects are judged against the published schema by ruling, and the two typed aliases the reader happens to bind are refused with their cure named.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **MUST-FIX — the ADR-0087 disposition (② above).** Escalated to the seat for which cure: a registered D2 conversion for the filter move (plus the D3 entry), or a ruled exemption written into the marker with the rewrite spelling removed. Both are edits to the changeset at least; the first is code.
- **Escalated — typed aliases the runtime binds are refused (ruling (a) mechanism vs its reason).** `{ type: 'interval', every }` and `{ type: 'cron', cron }` run today and are refused by the typed arm. The ruling's text sanctions the refusal; its stated reason does not. Corpus zero in both repos. The seat confirms the refusal stands (and the changeset sentence above is corrected), or carves the two typed aliases out. Not a must-fix: the behaviour follows the ruling as written.
- **Should-fix (follow-up card, `ui/**`, outside this PR's surface) — the Studio designer produces a refused draft.** `scheduleWithExpression` (`flow-node-config.ts:1710`) rewrites the whole `config.schedule` block on each cron edit; clearing the cron on a typed block leaves `{ type: 'cron' }` or `{ type: 'cron', timezone: 'UTC' }` (only an untyped `{ expression }` collapses to `undefined`), and the field's own help text says "A time-relative sweep defaults to daily if left empty". On `main` that draft stored and the schedule flow silently never bound (the sweep defaulted); on this head the draft save is refused 422 at `nodes.i.config.schedule` with the cure. The refusal is correct under ruling (a) and names the fix, so it is not blocking — but it is a draft-door refusal of a designer-authored intermediate shape, the exact reason item C moved to lint (the C changeset says so in its own words), and the designer should drop a typed block that no longer carries a cadence. The seat decides whether this is a follow-up card or an accepted behaviour; the PR body already declares drafts among the refusing doors.
- **Dev `open_questions`: none declared.** Flags carried from 6717473839: the full dispatch-gates set and the dogfood battery were not run on this head (seat asked for the fast set) — covered by CI below, `Dogfood Regression Gate` success; the full suites ran on a pre-restart tree — `Test Core` shards cover the head. Not named by the dev: the PR adds a test file under `packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/`, which the claim's file surface (6712039823) does not list ("⛔ runtime engines" is the nearest row). It is test-only, moves no runtime source and takes no changeset, so it is an undeclared but harmless deviation; the seat notes it.
- **Should-fix (wording): the `timeRelative: null` guard mismatch and the record-change/api `schedule` wording** (① above).
